title: The relational model: tables, rows, columns, and keys

questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “The relational model: tables, rows, columns, and keys”?
options: student_id identifies a student; the course_id/student_id pair identifies an enrollment.
The query returns Ada and 42 in two columns.
Start with a small, readable SELECT query; connect it to an application only after you understand its result.
SQLite often runs inside the application; MySQL and PostgreSQL commonly run as separate server processes.
questions.answer: student_id identifies a student; the course_id/student_id pair identifies an enrollment.
questions.explanation:
student_id identifies a student; the course_id/student_id pair identifies an enrollment.
Why: A relational database stores data in tables. A row is one record; a column is one attribute, and the schema defines column names and types. A primary key uniquely identifies a row; a foreign key links it to a row in another table. Connecting students and enrollments through student_id is safer than copying a student's details into every enrollment.
